instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 tbsp of the salt.
Meanwhile, dice the onion, slice the 8 oz mushrooms and mince the 2 garlic cloves. Pull or chop the 2 cups chicken into bite size pieces.
Add 8 oz of the spaghetti to the boiling water and cook it for 2 minutes less than the package says, so it's still a little firm in the middle. Drain it. It finishes cooking in the oven.

While the pasta cooks, heat the 1 tbsp olive oil in a large, deep skillet over medium high. Add the mushrooms in a single layer, sprinkle 1/4 tsp of the salt over them and leave them alone for 3 to 4 minutes, until they're browned underneath.
Stir the mushrooms and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until they're browned all over.

Turn the heat down to medium. Add the 2 tbsp butter and the onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is soft. Add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.
Sprinkle in the 3 tbsp flour and the 1 tsp Italian seasoning. Stir for 1 minute, until no dry flour shows.
Pour in the 1/3 cup wine and stir for about 30 seconds, until it thickens. Slowly pour in 1 cup of the broth and the 1 cup half-and-half, stirring as you go.
Bring it to a gentle boil and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the sauce is thick enough to coat a spoon.
Turn the heat to low. Add 4 oz of the cream cheese in small cubes, the remaining 3/4 tsp salt and the 1/4 tsp pepper. Stir until the cream cheese melts into the sauce.
Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the spaghetti, the chicken, 1/2 cup of the peas and 3/4 cup of the mozzarella until everything is coated.
Transfer it into a 2 quart baking dish and spread it out evenly. Cover the dish with foil and bake for 20 minutes.

Take off the foil. Sprinkle the remaining 3/4 cup mozzarella and the 1/4 cup Parmesan over the top. Bake it uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and golden at the edges and the sauce bubbles.
Leave it for 5 minutes, then serve.
method_notes: Both versions toss undercooked spaghetti and cooked chicken in a butter and flour sauce made with chicken broth and cream, then bake it in a casserole until hot. Spend With Pennies softens onion and mushrooms in the butter, adds white wine, half-and-half and Italian seasoning, melts cream cheese into the sauce, stirs in peas and bakes it covered for 20 minutes, then uncovered under mozzarella and Parmesan. Taste of Home uses canned mushrooms, pimientos and both half-and-half and heavy cream, tops it with Parmesan only and makes two casseroles, one for the freezer; its rating shows only a review count (21), not a rating count. This follows Spend With Pennies, cut to 8 oz pasta for 4, and browns fresh mushrooms in oil before the onion goes in.
